chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Ali ibn Rabat from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The brothers from the mother do not inherit anything from the blood money.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood money / Wergild (compensation paid for murder or injury)
key_terms.الْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Maternal brothers (half-brothers sharing the same mother)

ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that maternal brothers (ikhwān min al-umm) are excluded from inheriting the blood money (diyah) of a deceased relative, a ruling that distinguishes them from full or paternal brothers who typically share in the compensation. This specific exclusion highlights the nuanced application of inheritance principles in Shia jurisprudence, where the nature of the asset (diyah vs. estate) and the degree of kinship determine eligibility, often contrasting with general inheritance shares outlined in the Quran. The ruling underscores the scholarly tradition of differentiating between the distribution of the deceased's own property and the compensation received for their death.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala and Ali Bin Rabat, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The brothers from the mother do not inherit anything from the wergild’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah and Ali ibn Ribat from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
brothers from mother’s side do not receive any share from the wergild.’”
